title: Dimension at a point of a finite type algebra over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a prime ideal, with localization $S_{\mathfrak p}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak p$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim S_{\mathfrak p}$ the Krull dimension of the ring $S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then all three are finite and $$\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim S_{\mathfrak p}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p).$$

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00P1 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, line 28222); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00P1,algebra-lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field)

proof.text: Put $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The closed subspace $V(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ is the spectrum of the finite type domain $S/\mathfrak p$, and its fraction field is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim V(\mathfrak p)=r<\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring], every maximal chain of primes of $S/\mathfrak p$ has length $r$; equivalently, there is a maximal chain $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_r$ in $S$ starting at $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P1 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, lines 28238-28244), invoking Tags 00P0 and 00OS

proof.text: The finite type $k$-algebra $S$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so it has finitely many minimal prime ideals [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes]. Let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ be exactly those minimal primes contained in $\mathfrak p$; this list is nonempty because every prime contains a minimal prime. Under the order-preserving bijection between primes of $S_{\mathfrak p}$ and primes of $S$ contained in $\mathfrak p$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1), the $\mathfrak q_j$ correspond exactly to the minimal primes $\mathfrak q_jS_{\mathfrak p}$ of $S_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P1, lines 28245-28248; finiteness and nonemptiness are the Noetherian minimal-prime facts used implicitly there

proof.text: For each $j$, choose a maximal chain $\mathfrak q_j\subsetneq\mathfrak p'_{j,1}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p'_{j,s(j)}=\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] and the correspondence in Step 2, $$\dim S_{\mathfrak p}=\max_{1\le j\le t}s(j).$$ In particular this dimension is finite.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P1, lines 28249-28256

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components], $$\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\max_{1\le j\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_j).$$ For each $j$, concatenate the chain of Step 3 from $\mathfrak q_j$ to $\mathfrak p$ with the chain of Step 1 from $\mathfrak p$ upward. The result is a maximal chain in the finite type domain $S/\mathfrak q_j$ of length $s(j)+r$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring] therefore gives $\dim(S/\mathfrak q_j)=s(j)+r$. Taking maxima and using Step 3 yields $$\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=r+\max_js(j)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)+\dim S_{\mathfrak p}.$$ All three terms are finite by Steps 1 and 3.
